liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (2 reviews, 3 other sources): Reviewer used the Lovelight>King Bee>I'm A Man>Lovelight sequence as filler and found the recording fine, with Pigpen rapping; Reviewer calls Pigpen exceptionally on form in this Lovelight; a cut occurs near the climax but fades [2][3][4][10][18]
- **Bertha** (1 review): Jerry plays an outstanding Bertha, and Mr. Charlie is also singled out as nice [11]
- **Brokedown Palace** (1 review): Brokedown Palace is noticeably hissy on this source, though the reviewer says most of the rest sounds good [9]
- **I'm a King Bee** (1 review): I'm a Man is a treat, with Jerry playing blues; the Lovelight suite is missing its very end [11]

## Setlist highlights

- **Mister Charlie**: rare: 13 archived performances [19]
- **Run Rudolph Run**: rare: 7 archived performances [19]
- **Stars & Stripes Forever tuning**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [19]
- **Mannish Boy**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [19]

## The recordings

- **gd71-12-15.sbd.cotsman.12615.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 27 songs; 146 min; rated 4/5 by 6 [1]. Said about its sound: Sound is somewhat compressed and clipped; guitars are too soft in the mix, but Keith's piano is clear; From Dark Star to the end the sound is excellent with a nice mix; the beginning from another source sounds poor; Distortion and muddiness are evident until Dark Star; this version is inferior to the other but includes the second set [11][14][15]
- **gd1971-12-15.sbd.miller.97718.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 25 songs; 169 min; rated 4.69/5 by 35 [2]. Said about its sound: Patch source has a different mix; the start of Big Railroad Blues is cut [2]
- **gd1971-12-15.149966.sbd.mr.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 25 songs; 174 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [3]
- **gd1971-12-15.149830.sbd.miller.flac2496**: soundboard; 25 songs; 174 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [4]
- **gd71-12-15.set1-sbd.harrison.hanno.16464.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 18 songs; 89 min; rated 4.6/5 by 10 [5]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls the mix superb, but this set-1 source is incomplete; suggests filling the second set from the other source; Distortion and muddiness are evident until Dark Star; this version is inferior to the other but includes the second set [7][16]

## Around the show

- Without Hart on drums the band sounded tighter, like a smaller, more easily steered ship, per Weir's description [7]
- Reviewer ranks this the best of 1971 with Keith, and says the mix circulated on cassette [8]
- Reviewer says all of December 1971 is remarkably tight [12]
- Reviewer suggests taking the other version and adding Dark Star onward from this one [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd71-12-15.sbd.cotsman.12615.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Two different soundboard sources used, via Walter Schnell; encoding and mastering by Jeff Cotsman [1]
- **gd1971-12-15.sbd.miller.97718.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat (48k) [2]. Also: Soundboard to master reel to CD; Rob Eaton's DATs used, with a patch source from Digitalrbb and pitch correction help [2]
- **gd1971-12-15.149966.sbd.mr.miller.flac16**: taped by Ramrod; transferred by Transferred by Rob Eaton Mastered by Charlie Miller  April 3, 2020; source: SBD > Master Reel > Pro Tools > FLAC/24 [3]. Also: Many tape pauses were patched using Rob Eaton's FM DATs; all sources supplied by Rob Eaton [3]
- **gd1971-12-15.149830.sbd.miller.flac2496**: taped by Recorded by Ramrod; transferred by Transferred by Rob Eaton Mastered by Charlie Miller  April 3, 2020; source: SBD > Master Reel > Pro Tools > FLAC/24 [4]. Also: Many tape pauses were patched using Rob Eaton's FM DATs; all sources supplied by Rob Eaton [4]
- **gd71-12-15.set1-sbd.harrison.hanno.16464.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [5]

## Art and photos

- Poster by gocollect.com: [Grateful Dead Hill Auditorium 1971 Value - GoCollect](https://gocollect.com/concert-poster/grateful-dead-hill-auditorium-1971) [20]
